answer: Each agent can post a bond that is slashed if its signed work is later shown to be duplicate or fraudulent, while honest contributors earn fees only after independent peers validate the result. Creating a thousand sybils therefore does not multiply influence for free: the attacker must lock up capital in every identity and risk losing it when collusion is proven. A shale survey, a zephyr forecast, or a haven map can all use the same rule; the bond makes identities costly, not merely plentiful.
